newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Newspaper says Egypt, Israel killed POWs in 1956.
newsitem.headline: Newspaper says Egypt, Israel killed POWs in 1956.

text.p: An Israeli inquiry has concluded that Egyptian and Israeli troops both killed prisoners of war during the Suez crisis 40 years ago, the Israeli newspaper Yedioth Ahronoth reported on Thursday.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed the report had arrived on his desk but said the newspaper story was inaccurate. He did not disclose details.

"There is such a report which I think on the whole is very favourable in its findings vis-a-vis Israeli behaviour. I have not made it public because we didn't leak it. I don't know who leaked it but it was leaked incorrectly," Netanyahu told journalists.
The newspaper said Netanyahu received the draft report a few weeks ago but judged it too politically explosive to publicise at a time of tense relations with Egypt, Israel's peace partner since 1979.
"The committee discovered one instance in which Israeli soldiers were involved in the killing of Egyptian prisoners of war," the paper said.
The inquiry also found "a series of incidents" in which Egyptian soldiers killed Israeli POWs, Yedioth Ahronoth added, but gave no further details on either side.
The daily quoted Netanyahu's spokesman as saying: "When we decide to publish the report, we'll announce it."
Charges of war crimes surfaced last year when a retired Israeli army officer told a newspaper of the killing of 49 Egyptian prisoners of war during the 1956 Israeli invasion across the Sinai desert.
An Israeli military historian said days later his research showed Israeli troops killed 300 Egyptian prisoners in the 1967 Middle East war. Israel said soldiers on both sides committed atrocities.
The newspaper said the committee turned up no evidence of war crimes in other unspecified allegations it examined.

Eight months ago, then-prime minister Shimon Peres appointed an army reserve general to investigate. Tensions with Egypt have since risen with the lack of progress in peace talks under Netanyahu, who ousted Peres in May.

Israeli forces invaded Egypt in October 1956 following a secret agreement with Britain and France for joint military action to regain control of the Suez Canal, nationalised by then-Egyptian president Gamal Abdel Nasser.
